job.title: SVP, Product
job.description:
The big picture: Axios is a media company built around clarity, trust, and smart, essential coverage. As AI reshapes how companies operate, Axios has an opportunity to become more AI-native in how we build products, improve workflows, and help teams move faster with better judgment.

Axios is hiring an SVP, Product to lead how Axios builds products across the company, strengthening Product and Design while turning promising AI-enabled ideas into durable, supported products.

Why it matters: Axios builds and ships at multiple levels. Product and Design lead the development of durable, company-wide products and shared platforms. AI Enablement partners with departments to identify opportunities, prototype AI-enabled tools and workflows, and help teams put useful solutions into practice.

The SVP, Product will connect these levels by making decision rights, prioritization, and handoffs clear: what should remain a local workflow, what AI Enablement should support, and what Product and Design should develop into a durable, supported product or shared capability. The role spans the products, platforms, and workflows that power Axios, from the CMS, axios.com, newsletters, and Local products to internal tools and shared platforms supporting editorial, revenue, and company operations, as well as the growing set of AI-enabled solutions being developed closer to the work.

As Axios becomes more capable of building with AI, more teams will identify and prototype solutions for their own needs. This leader will establish the product operating model that allows Axios to evaluate, prioritize, and scale those ideas without creating fragmented, duplicated, or unsupported systems.

What you’ll do:

  • Lead Product, Design, and AI Enablement, setting strategy, priorities, decision rights, and operating cadence.
  • Look ahead: turn a clear point of view on emerging technologies, behaviors, and opportunities into credible product choices and experiments.
  • Partner with business leaders to translate company and functional goals into clear product opportunities, outcomes, and investment choices.
  • Raise the product management bar through clear expectations, coaching, and accountability.
  • Create a clear path from promising experiments to durable, supported products.

Go deeper: This leader must be a trusted partner to senior leaders, with a clear point of view on where technology is moving, the confidence to challenge assumptions, and the judgment to turn ambiguity into decisions.

Success means a clear company-wide model for deciding what Axios should build and why, stronger and faster Product and Design decisions, and a repeatable path from promising AI experiments to durable, supported products.

What we’re looking for:

  • A trusted partner to senior leaders who can challenge assumptions, form a clear point of view, make hard tradeoffs, and keep decisions moving.
  • A clear vision for where product development is headed and how Axios can succeed as the technology landscape rapidly evolves.
  • Demonstrated AI fluency: you personally use AI to accelerate your work and prototype ideas, and you know how to turn AI capabilities into useful products and workflows.
  • Senior product leadership experience in software, information services, media, or another fast-moving environment, with a record of bringing Product and Design together.
  • Technical fluency across product strategy, workflows, tooling, data, and production tradeoffs.
  • Experience with prioritization and portfolio management across multiple stakeholders.
  • A track record of turning prototypes and experiments into durable, supported products.
  • The judgment to create useful governance without becoming a bottleneck.
  • The ability to distinguish a meaningful product opportunity from an interesting AI demo.

Worth your time: This is an opportunity to help define what modern product leadership looks like inside an AI-native media company. You’ll help shape not only what Axios builds, but how Axios operates.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-10-11 11:59 PM

Your Role


As the Administrative Officer, you are an essential part of the Payments and Broadcast Contract Administration (PACD) team. You are responsible for handling a wide range of administrative tasks related to contract management and compliance for the broader Business & Rights (BR) team within CBC/Radio-Canada French Services. 


As the Administrative Office, you are part of Radio-Canada's French-language Management of Rights and Business Relations team, which is responsible for negotiating agreements for the acquisition and production of content to be broadcast on Radio-Canada's platforms.


As an Administrative officer you report to the Manager, Contract Operations and Administration, and are responsible for supporting and working closely with project managers by performing administrative tasks related to the conclusion of agreements. To do so, the administrative officer must enter contractual information such as rights, licensing costs, and broadcast obligations into the contract and rights management system and prepare contractual documents (letters, contracts, amendments, or recommendations) and payment tables.


As an Administrative officer, you are also responsible for coordinating approvals and signatures on contractual documents and ensuring the compliance of data entered into the tools used by Radio-Canada. Finally, this role involves collaboration with internal partners, independent producers, and international distributors. 


Function:

Analyze and report on the Corporation’s position and alternatives in selected administrative matters to see how well departmental strategies are being applied, as well as to support decision-making and planning. 


Key Tasks:

  • Interpret administrative standards, policies and procedures governing the management of budgets, insurance policies, leases, productivity, acquisitions, sales and other business matters, in order to resolve issues that arise in processing or analyzing the related data.
  • Monitor changes in contracts, estimates and the market; provide commentary on performance and services rendered; and identify trends in order to report, at any time or for any period, the Corporation’s progress in implementing management strategies (by identifying gaps or alternatives, producing projections, advising managers in preparing or correcting timelines, etc.).
  • Negotiate a variety of service contracts and leases within established parameters, providing key administrative support for departmental activities; initiate more significant negotiations by gathering requests, offers and all necessary documents, including comparative data and reports, ahead of time; identify and highlight market trends, standards and related practices to inform the negotiation process.
  • Complete the appropriate forms and documents; prepare the necessary correspondence and reports based on available information, following up as required.
  • Familiarize other people with their job by explaining your own duties.
  • Perform all other administrative tasks.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.


What You Bring:


Qualifications: 

  • College diploma in a relevant field (e.g., management, administration).
  • At least two (2) years’ experience in a related field (administration in a unionized environment).

Skills:

  • Ability to manage priorities, be organized and work well under tight deadlines.
  • Ability to be thorough, meticulous, accurate, resourceful, discreet, concise, curious and adapt easily to new computer tools.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication and teamwork skills.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and the MS Office suite.
  • Solid command of spoken and written French (working language).
  • Knowledge of English (asset).

 

Selected candidates will be tested as follows:

  • Interview.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
 

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

As part of our recruitment process, candidates who advance to the next

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-09-30 11:59 PM

This is a nine (9) month contract position.


Working alongside the Promotion and Digital Entertainment teams, you will gather requirements, and define and lead Radio-Canada’s French-language digital strategy for the Eurovision Song Contest. 


Working in alignment with Digital Entertainment initiatives, you will co-ordinate the rollout of marketing and content plans across digital and social media platforms. You will leverage data, promotional opportunities and strategic content partnerships to achieve two primary objectives: 

  • Maximize live viewership among French-speaking Canadians.
  • Maximize audience engagement and participation during the national voting phase to select Canada’s representative, while mobilizing domestic and international support for Canada’s artist during the main competition. 

This role serves as the primary liaison between teams across Radio-Canada, CBC and the European Broadcasting Union (EBU).


Key Responsibilities:


Digital Marketing Strategy:

  • Liaise with the CRM and strategy teams to ensure co-ordinated and aligned messaging. 
  • Design audience journeys that convert awareness into engagement, engagement into votes and votes into live viewership.
  • Tailor strategies across each project phase: call for submissions, artist selection, public voting, winner announcement, competition preparation and the live broadcast.
  • Maintain consistent messaging, content, calls to action and timelines across all touchpoints.

Website and Voting Platform:

  • Define the content and engagement strategy for Radio-Canada’s Eurovision website.
  • Plan required content and features for the public voting window (October 8-18).
  • Help draft the request for proposals (RFP) for the digital voting solution.
  • Collaborate on selecting, implementing, testing and launching the voting platform.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams spanning editorial, marketing, product, technology, data, security and legal.
  • Maintain a fast, reliable flow of information regarding submissions, artists, announcements and results.
  • Manage tracking and conversion requirements to activate website and platform audience data.
  • Oversee data synchronization between collection platforms and audience activation systems in collaboration with technical specialists.

Data and Relationship Marketing:

  • Work with the CRM team to engage and re-engage audiences via newsletters, push notifications and targeted communications aligned with the project’s relationship marketing strategy. 

Social Media and Content:

  • Develop the overarching French-language social media strategy for the project.
  • Establish editorial guidelines, content formats, publication schedules and engagement tactics.
  • Plan promotional content designed to expand reach, drive participation and boost live viewership.
  • Co-ordinate content production across TV, audio and digital teams.
  • Map out content needs for each phase: artist reveals, behind-the-scenes access, voting guides, community outreach, result announcements and final preparations.
  • Ensure Radio-Canada and CBC content complement each other seamlessly.
  • Identify opportunities to adapt, share or co-produce content with CBC and the EBU.

Content Creators and Influencers:

  • Develop a collaboration strategy for relevant content creators and influencers.
  • Define their role in driving artist discovery, building community support, encouraging voting and promoting the live broadcast.
  • Align organic and paid creator campaigns with broader marketing efforts.
  • Ensure all partnerships comply with Radio-Canada’s brand positioning and competition rules.

Project Management:

  • Build and maintain the master schedule for all digital activities.
  • Co-ordinate announcements, approvals, deliverables and communications across all stakeholders.
  • Identify dependencies, mitigate risks, track pending decisions and ensure timely followup.
  • Lead co-ordination meetings and produce concise decision logs.
  • Foster close collaboration with the CBC and EBU teams.
  • Supervise a Digital Editor responsible for creating, adapting, integrating and publishing promotional and editorial content that meets Content and Marketing team needs.
  • Ensure projects adhere to schedules, budgets, quality standards and approval workflows.

Performance Indicators:


Your performance will be evaluated based on the following key metrics:


Contribution to Organizational Objectives:

  • Total French-speaking Canadian live viewership numbers.
  • Traffic and engagement across Radio-Canada digital destinations, including overall voting participation volume.

Specific KPIs:

  • Social media reach, engagement and community growth.
  • Subscriber growth across newsletters, push notifications and other CRM channels.
  • Content performance and influencer collaboration metrics.
  • Adherence to schedules, budgets and technical milestones.
  • Quality of co-ordination between Radio-Canada, CBC, the EBU and external partners.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines. 


What You Bring:

  • Minimum seven (7) years’ experience in digital project management, social media strategy or digital marketing.
  • University degree in marketing, communications, business administration or a related field.
  • Proven track record of planning and delivering high-profile integrated campaigns.
  • Deep understanding of web platforms, social media ecosystems, relationship marketing, data analytics and user journeys.
  • Ability to manage cross-functional editorial, marketing, technical and creative teams simultaneously.
  • Experience implementing digital platforms or evaluating technical RFPs.
  • Exceptional planning, prioritization and schedule management skills.
  • Ability to make prompt, sound decisions in a fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environment.
  • Strong analytical skills focused on performance tracking and continuous optimization.
  • Excellent communication skills in French, with the ability to collaborate effectively in English.
  • Knowledge of the media, entertainment, music or live events industries is an asset.

Core Competencies:

  • Strategic vision.
  • Cross-functional leadership.
  • Project management.
  • Editorial and marketing co-ordination.
  • Content strategy.
  • Social media expertise.
  • Audience- and results-focused mindset.
  • Data analysis.
  • Operational excellence.
  • Collaboration and influence.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

As part of our recruitment process, candidates who advance to the next

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.

Are you passionate about change management and bringing organizations through the project process from conception to adoption? In this role, you'll support the Digital Products and Innovation team (PIN/DP&I) in developing and delivering engagement initiatives focused on change and transformation.

 

Reporting to the Senior Director, Digital Operations, you'll join the Digital Products and Innovation team (PIN/DP&I) where a major initiative is underway to modernize CBC/Radio-Canada’s digital ecosystem and make it more resilient in an evolving media environment. This exciting work will be done in close cooperation with various departments and will greatly contribute to build the public broadcaster’s future.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling, and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams.

 

When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.


This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.


Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in developing complex and high-performance mobile applications.
  • Proficiency in Android Studio, Git, and the Kotlin language.
  • Experience in developing an application published on Google Play.
  • Experience in developing within code review context (pull request).
  • Knowledge of programming patterns (such as MVP or MVVM).
  • Knowledge of SOLID architecture principles is an asset.
  • Ability to read, produce, and adhere to software architecture diagrams (UML, sequence diagram, etc.).
  • Interest in working on an application available on multiple form factors (mobile/tablet/TV).
  • Knowledge of Jetpack Compose, Exoplayer, Kotlin Multiplatform is an asset.
  • Knowledge of the libraries Dagger, Hilt, Koin is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Google architecture components is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Maven (including the design/maintenance of internal libraries) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.

 

Please note this is a 12-month contract position, renewable annually. This regular position is not a consulting assignment but a long-term opportunity with attractive CBC/Radio-Canada employee benefits.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.

The Regional Media team is seeking a Digital Operations Producer to modernize and streamline workflows across our regional stations nationwide.


Reporting to the Manager, Content Development and Production, you will fulfil a vital, newly created role as the national point of contact responsible for evaluating emerging technologies, standardizing practices and driving operational deployment in the field. By scaling successful local initiatives into network-wide standards, you will eliminate redundant efforts and build strong connections among regional experts to foster continuous knowledge sharing.


Bridging technology strategy and daily operations, you will guide teams toward efficient, audience-focused practices and establish new, digital-first standards and workflows tailored to an evolving media landscape.


You will have the autonomy to exercise leadership, judgment and initiative to embed a culture of agility and innovation across the network.

  • Design, develop and implement efficient digital production processes tailored to the unique needs of Radio-Canada regional stations while aligning with overall strategic priorities.
  • Plan, organize and co-ordinate user training and professional development programs on media production tools and workflows.
  • Partner with regional teams to execute pilot projects testing and evaluating new production methods.
  • Develop vendor relationships and draft technical specifications.
  • Foster strong, collaborative partnerships across divisions, including T&I, News, Digital Products, Innovation, Audio and CBC teams.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.


This role can be based in the following locations: Ottawa, Edmonton, Regina, Sudbury, Toronto, Vancouver or Winnipeg.

Your Role

 

The Director, AI Governance and Adoption is responsible for driving the evolution of the enterprise AI governance framework, and facilitating the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence technologies across the organization. Acting as a strategic partner to executives and business teams, this individual supports the identification of opportunities, the integration of value-creating solutions and the development of an AI-literate culture. The incumbent also oversees the development of the practices, policies and governance mechanisms required to ensure the responsible and sustainable use of artificial intelligence technologies.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Governance, Policy & Risk Management

  • Define and enforce corporate AI policies, directives, and guardrails across all business units.
  • Operationalize risk controls and decision accountabilities across the entire AI lifecycle (procurement, data retrieval, tool actions, and human oversight).
  • Build and maintain a central inventory of all internal and third-party AI assets to track systemic risk.

 

Shadow AI & Secure Experimentation

  • Audit unsanctioned AI tools ("shadow AI") across departments and facilitate the transition of use cases into secure enterprise environments.
  • Partner with tech teams to set safety guardrails for low-code/no-code tools, allowing employees to experiment safely.

 

Leadership, Committees & Alignment

  • Lead the AI Usage Oversight Committee and coordinate the enterprise AI Steering Committee.
  • Align AI initiatives with Legal, Privacy, InfoSec, Data Governance, and Journalistic Standards to ensure regulatory compliance.

 

Adoption, Enablement & Literacy

  • Develop training programs, playbooks, office hours, and champion networks to boost organization-wide AI literacy.
  • Help business units integrate deployed AI solutions into their everyday production workflows.

 

Workflow Re-Engineering & Value Tracking

  • Direct a cross-functional "Fusion Team" to help management re-engineer legacy workflows for native AI integration.
  • Define, track, and report performance and governance metrics to prove ROI and accountability.

 

Vendor Management & Industry Representation

  • Advise Procurement and Legal on standards for evaluating and onboarding third-party AI vendors.
  • Represent the organization (CBC/Radio-Canada) at national and international conferences, contributing to public media data provenance standards.

 

Internal Governance & Executive Alignment

  • Senior Advisory: Advise executives on AI strategy, run governance committees, and deliver executive leadership-level briefings when required.
  • Standards & Training: Roll out AI policies across all departments (Media, Tech, Business) and partner with L&D on staff training and literacy initiatives.

 

AI Adoption & Change Management

  • Fusion Team Leadership: Stand up and lead a cross-functional team of change management, training, and process optimization specialists.
  • Workflow Integration: Work with department heads and staff to resolve workflow pain points and drive adoption of approved AI tools.
  • Tracking & Reporting: Partner with Innovation Leads to establish ROI metrics and report adoption progress, blockers, and learnings to leadership.

 

External Relations & Industry Networks

  • Industry and Peer Collaboration: Partner with media organizations, industry groups (EBU, INMA), and analysts (Gartner) to benchmark best practices.
  • Thought Leadership: Share CBC/RC case studies and governance frameworks with external and public stakeholders.

 

What You Bring

 

Qualifications, experience & skills

  • 7+ years of technology leadership experience, with 3 years of supervisory experience required.
  • At least 5 years explicitly focused on operationalizing data or technology strategy, machine learning, technology risk management, or corporate governance programs.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required. A degree in Information Technology, Computer Systems Analysis, Engineering, or Management Information Systems is preferred.
  • Bilingualism (English and French).
  • Enterprise AI Governance: Proven track record building and managing AI oversight programs, governing models and agentic workflows, and developing policies, audits, and control documentation.
  • Strategy-to-Operations: Ability to turn high-level strategy into actionable standards, operational workflows, and scalable operating models.
  • Enterprise Change & Adoption: Demonstrated success scaling technology adoption across matrixed, multi-stakeholder organizations.
  • AI & Data Expertise: Deep knowledge of AI lifecycles, generative/agentic risks, data privacy, and public media compliance standards.
  • Executive Leadership: Exceptional communication skills to translate complex AI concepts and risks into business impact for executive and board-level stakeholders.

Role

 

As the Director, Digital Delivery Portfolio, you will help shape the future of digital media in Canada. Reporting to the Senior Director, Operations and Digital Delivery Portfolio, you will foster dynamic collaboration across Digital Products & Innovation (DP&I) teams at both CBC and Radio-Canada.

 

In this role, you will oversee our portfolio of digital programs and initiatives, ensuring they are perfectly aligned with our strategic ambitions. Acting as an architect of change, you will explore opportunities presented by artificial intelligence (AI) while leveraging agile and project management methodologies to maximize value and impact. Your continuous improvement expertise will be vital to optimizing budget management, driving performance, boosting efficiency and maintaining high service quality.

 

You will lead a team of passionate professionals, including executives, project leads and business analysts, inspiring them toward excellence. Your sharp analytical skills and strategic judgment will empower you to navigate complex challenges, formulate impactful recommendations and make decisions that will shape the future of our component and the organization as a whole.

 

You will also ensure that leadership teams and all key stakeholders receive relevant updates on project progress.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain a scalable project and program management and governance structure aligned with our product lines and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement by developing and refining operational processes.
  • Manage a strategic portfolio of project and program management services for DP&I, from initial analysis through to execution and delivery.
  • Produce regular reporting, including performance indicators and metrics, executive summaries and ad hoc analysis.
  • Work closely with the Finance and Operations team.
  • Provide close oversight of initiative and program budgets and costs, as well as resource allocation.
  • Proactively evaluate shifting functional needs, capacity constraints, risk management and interdependencies.

  • Serve as a change management agent to facilitate adoption within a rapidly evolving media landscape.
  • Communicate the status of the project and program portfolio to stakeholders across all business units.
  • Deliver on business objectives while maintaining exceptional service quality.

 

This role is based in Toronto.

We want to hear about your unique background! It is essential that you submit an up-to-date resumé highlighting your skills and qualifications, and demonstrating why you are a great fit for this role.

  • Project management and agile certification desirable.
  • Agile experience an asset.

  • Experience coaching teams using Lean and/or Kanban methodologies an asset.
  • At least 10 years’ experience working in Agile environments with collaboration tools such as Jira and Confluence.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.


Your Role

 

In an environment where data has become a critical strategic asset supporting decision-making, advanced analytics and artificial intelligence solutions, CBC/Radio-Canada is implementing an enterprise-wide data governance program. The creation of the Director, Enterprise Data Governance role is at the heart of this transformation and aims to establish the foundations required for the effective, secure and consistent management of information assets.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Framework, Policies & Compliance

  • Develop, refine, and enforce enterprise-wide data governance policies, directives, and standards aligned with corporate priorities.
  • Work with Legal, InfoSec, and Data Engineering to establish data classification rules, access controls, and compliance monitoring.
  • Define core data concepts and maintain central governance documentation and artifacts.

 

Core Programs & Data Operations

  • Data Catalog & Metadata: Oversee the implementation of an enterprise data catalog and metadata management processes to ensure reporting mechanisms and datasets are clear and accessible.
  • Data Quality & Lineage: Stand up an enterprise data quality program and implement data lineage tracking to monitor how data moves across systems.
  • Usability & AI Readiness: Partner with technology and analytics teams to make sure data is clean and structured for BI, reporting, and AI/ML models.

 

Governance Bodies & Stakeholder Leadership

  • Manage the Enterprise Data Governance Steering Committee to align senior leadership on strategic priorities.
  • Lead the Enterprise Data Council (domain leads and Data Officers) to translate strategic directives into policies and actionable initiatives.
  • Drive the creation of cross-functional networks of data stewards, owners, custodians, and working groups as needed.

 

Data Literacy & Culture

  • Lead change management, training, and communication programs to improve overall data literacy across the corporation.
  • Influence senior executives and business stakeholders to adopt governance practices and understand their role in protecting and using data.
  • Build, mentor, and lead a small, high-impact data governance team.

 

Metrics, KPI Tracking & Reporting                       

  • Define, track, and report on core governance KPIs, including data quality, issue resolution, policy compliance, and user adoption.
  • Build and maintain executive dashboards to regularly report program progress and outcomes to leadership.

 

What You Bring

 

Qualifications, experience & skills

  • 5+ years of experience in data management, governance, or a related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field.
  • Proven experience building and launching enterprise data governance programs.
  • Experience leading enterprise-grade data catalog / data governance tooling initiatives.
  • Experience developing and managing a business glossary.
  • Experience operating in a national, matrixed organization.
  • Bilingualism (English and French).

 

Technical:

  • Core Skills & Technical Proficiencies: Strong hands-on experience with SQL, data modeling, structured/unstructured data governance, and ETL/ELT logic. Profiency  withPython, Jira, and workflow mapping tools is a key asset.
  • Governance Tooling & Platforms: Hands-on experience with integrating and/or heavy use of enterprise data governance tools (e.g., Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Purview) and familiarity with major cloud-based data platforms (e.g.: Google Cloud Platform, Azure).
  • Data Lifecycle & Quality Operations: Proven track record in building and validating data lineage, managing data quality validation/remediation, and creating or overseeing automated scripts for metadata harvesting and validation.
  • Architecture & Team Collaboration: Deep understanding of modern data architectures (cloud data platforms, BI/analytics, AI/ML pipelines) paired with a strong ability to collaborate across technical, product, vendor, and business teams.
  • Communication & Technical Translation: Exceptional ability to translate complex technical, architectural, and regulatory concepts into clear, actionable business language.
  • Nice-to-Have Technical Assets: Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and API-based metadata harvesting.

 

Non-technical:

  • Ability to understand and communicate the value of data as an asset.
  • Ability to manage cross-functional teams.
  • Business and technical requirements documentation skills.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Excellent communication and facilitation abilities.
  • Ability to lead by influence and work across teams and business units at varying levels of data governance maturity.

Reporting to the Executive Director, People Systems & Analytics the Director, People Analytics will own the vision, creation, and deployment of the enterprise-wide People Analytics strategy for CBC/Radio-Canada.

As a key strategic partner to executive leadership across the corporation, you will champion a data-driven culture, turning complex workforce data into actionable business intelligence that shapes our talent strategy and drives organizational performance. You will lead the maturation of our analytics function from descriptive reporting to predictive modeling, maximizing our investment in Workday to drive leader self-service while enforcing the highest standards of data governance and privacy.

Leading and scaling a dedicated team of Managers and Analytics Specialists, you will cultivate a team capable of diagnosing complex organizational needs and translating data into compelling, executive-level narratives that drive change.


Location: This is a bilingual position (English/French) and can be based in either Ottawa or Toronto with flexible hybrid work options.


Key Responsibilities and Projects:

Strategic Leadership & Vision


  • Own the Strategy: Develop, champion, and execute the multi-year People Analytics roadmap aligned with CBC/Radio-Canada’s overarching business and talent goals.
  • Executive Partnership: Act as the primary trusted advisor to business leaders and P&C executives, translating workforce trends, attrition models, and engagement data into high-impact business strategies.
  • Data Demoralization: Drive the adoption of leader self-service models to put data directly into the hands of decision-makers.

Data Governance & Ecosystem Management


  • Enterprise Governance: Architect and enforce strict data governance, data security, and privacy frameworks across all HR data systems, ensuring compliance with federal and internal privacy regulations.
  • Cross-Functional Integration: Partner with IT, Finance, and Corporate Research to break down data silos, integrating HR data with financial and operational KPIs to measure true business impact.

Scope of Impact:


  • Enterprise-wide People Analytics strategy

Decision Making Authority:

  • Define and lead the direction of the People Analytics program to meet the overall People & Culture strategy

Relationships:


  • This role would have to interact with all COE’s within People & Culture as well as key clients within other components, particularly, Finance, T&I, Media Lines
  • Exposure to SET members, unions and other key stakeholders as required

Leadership:


  • Foster a team culture of coaching and guiding process owners on the optimal, effective usage of Workday and other HR solutions to gain the most out of our technology by proactively recommending solutions to solve business needs or support their strategy.
  • People Leadership: Lead, mentor, and scale a high-performing team of data analysts and translators, fostering a culture of innovation, continuous learning, and consultative service excellence.
  • Advanced Storytelling: Oversee the design and evolution of enterprise HR dashboards and executive presentations, ensuring the team excels at "storytelling through data" to influence organizational health metrics.


Qualifications, Experience and Skills:


  • Education: University degree in Business Analytics, Statistics, Data Science, Human Resources, Organizational Development, or a related quantitative field (Master’s degree or MBA preferred).
  • Experience: 7+ years of progressive experience in business intelligence, data analytics, or HR strategy, with at least 10+ years in a distinct leadership role managing analytics teams within a complex, matrixed, or public-sector organization.
  • Platform Expertise: Proven experience leveraging enterprise HRIS platforms (Workday experience required) alongside advanced business intelligence tools (e.g., PowerBI, Data warehouse, data lakes, etc).
  • Language: Fully bilingual in English and French (written and spoken) is required.

Technical & Leadership Competencies


  • Strategic Problem Solving & Decision Making: Demonstrates the ability to navigate ambiguity and diagnose complex, systemic organizational challenges. Anticipates potential roadblocks, evaluates risks, and collaborates across functional boundaries to implement sustainable, data-driven solutions that align with long-term business goals. 
  • Predictive & Statistical Acumen: Strong foundational knowledge of statistical methods (e.g., regression analysis, forecasting, workforce modeling) and how to apply them to talent acquisition, retention, and diversity initiatives.
  • Data Governance Champion: Demonstrated experience building data governance frameworks, data dictionaries, and security protocols from scratch.
  • Executive Presence & Storytelling: Exceptional capability to connect abstract data points to concrete business outcomes, delivering compelling presentations to C-suite and Board-level stakeholders.

Working Conditions:

Reporting to the Executive Director, People Systems & Analytics, we are seeking a visionary and results-driven Director, Product Evolution (Workday) to lead the strategic advancement, configuration, and continuous improvement of our enterprise People & Culture technology ecosystem, including Workday and integrated third-party solutions.  


In this role, you will champion the lifecycle of our Workday product features, ensuring they align with broader business objectives and deliver maximum value to the organization.


You will lead, mentor, and scale a high-performing, cross-functional team of Business Analysts and Product Owners. As the bridge between business strategy and technical execution, you will own the Workday product evolution roadmap, investment alignment, governance and drive the end-to-end project management of feature rollouts, system optimizations, and semi-annual Workday releases.


Location: This is a bilingual position (English/French) and can be based in either Ottawa or Toronto with flexible hybrid work options.


Key Responsibilities


Strategic Leadership & Roadmap Management


  • Own the Evolution Roadmap: Define, manage, and execute the multi-year product evolution roadmap for the Workday platform and third party system integrations, balancing business-critical enhancements with technical debt and scalability.
  • Feature Evolution: Direct the evaluation, testing, and deployment of new Workday features, modules, and functionalities (including Workday’s semi-annual release cycles).
  • Stakeholder Alignment: Provide enterprise leadership and guidance by collaborating with People & Culture colleagues, Finance, IT, and other business units to translate organizational pain points into scalable technical solutions.

Team Management & Capability Building


  • Lead Cross-Functional Teams: Guide a dedicated team of Managers, Workday Business Analysts and Specialists, fostering a culture of agility, accountability, continuous learning and consultative service excellence.
  • Resource Allocation: Manage team capacity and prioritize incoming business requests against strategic platform goals.
  • Mentorship: Elevate the team’s capabilities in business analysis, Workday configuration best practices, and agile delivery methodologies.


Platform Performance, Risk & Compliance


  • Accountable for the stabilization, performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of enterprise People & Culture platforms.
  • Ensures system controls, audit readiness, compliance, and risk mitigation across P&C technology environments.
  • Establishes and monitors performance metrics to ensure operational effectiveness and value realization.

Delivery & Project Management


  • End-to-End PM Execution: Take full accountability for the project management lifecycle of Workday evolution initiatives—from initial scoping and requirements gathering to testing, change management, and deployment, in collaboration with People & Culture Centres of Expertise and other business units.
  • Governance & Compliance: Establish and maintain robust governance frameworks for Workday configurations, ensuring strict adherence to data privacy, security, and compliance standards.
  • Vendor & Partner Management: Act as a point of contact for Workday account teams, implementation partners, and third-party vendors.

About You


Required Skills & Experience


  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Human Resources, Information Technology, or related field
  • Workday Expertise: 7+ years of experience working closely with the Workday platform (Core HR, Benefits, Absence, Time Tracking, Payroll, Compensation, Talent), with a deep understanding of its architecture, business processes, and configuration capabilities.
  • Leadership Experience: 10+ years of experience directly managing and developing cross-functional teams of Business Analysts, Product Managers, or Systems Consultants.
  • Roadmap & Project Ownership: Proven track record of owning product roadmaps and successfully delivering complex, enterprise-level system implementations or evolution files.
  • Agile/PM Methodologies: Strong proficiency in project management frameworks (Agile, Scrum, or Waterfall) and tools (e.g., Jira, Service Now, etc).
  • Language: Fully bilingual in English and French (written and spoken) is required.

Technical & Leadership Competencies


  • Strategic Problem Solving & Decision Making: Demonstrates the ability to navigate ambiguity and diagnose complex, systemic organizational challenges. Anticipates potential roadblocks, evaluates risks, and collaborates across functional boundaries to implement sustainable, data-driven solutions that align with long-term business goals. 
  • Strategic Thinker, Tactical Doer: Ability to conceptualize the big picture while remaining grounded enough to oversee complex configuration dependencies.
  • Exceptional Communication: A knack for translating dense, technical Workday configurations into clear, value-driven business language for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Change Champion: Resilience and adaptability in a fast-paced environment, with a passion for driving user adoption and continuous process improvement.
  • Continuous Improvement: Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodologies considered an asset.  Strong knowledge of Human Resources processes and programs is considered an asset.

Position Overview


As a member of the Radio-Canada Marketing & Communications team, the Eurovision 360 Project Manager leads the planning, execution and co-ordination of all marketing initiatives celebrating Canada’s debut in the Eurovision Song Contest. In this role, you will oversee the creation and production of advertising and promotional assets, help shape marketing strategy and execute internal and external media plans. You will also collaborate closely with teams across CBC and Radio-Canada to align campaign goals company-wide.


Your Key Responsibilities:

  • Brief creative teams and manage advertising and promotional asset production, partnering with designers, directors and production staff to ensure high-quality, efficient delivery that meets established marketing goals.
  • Work closely with the Marketing Strategy team to deploy campaigns effectively in line with corporate objectives.
  • Help develop creative briefs and ensure alignment among all project stakeholders.
  • Ensure that all creative team deliverables align with Eurovision brand guidelines and Radio-Canada standards.
  • Oversee end-to-end production of communications and promotional collateral (video, audio, print, digital and experiential).
  • Co-ordinate all project logistics, including gathering client requirements, estimating costs, obtaining quotes, setting timelines, tracking team availability and securing necessary approvals.
  • Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to deliver projects that achieve strategic marketing objectives. 
  • Address challenges with project participants, recommend solutions and provide timely updates on project progress or changes.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications or a related field.
  • Five (5) or more years’ experience in project management within advertising or promotional production environments. 

Skills:

  • Deep understanding of production workflows for on-air promos and advertisements in all formats across broadcast, digital and external platforms.
  • Proven ability to plan, organize and prioritize projects.
  • Good knowledge of Radio-Canada’s network and advertising ecosystem.
  • Ability to be versatile, flexible, independent and adaptable to change.
  • Excellent organizational skills, thoroughness, tact and a collaborative mindset.
  • Excellent command of spoken and written French.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling, and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities  connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams.

 

When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.

 

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in developing complex and high-performance mobile applications.
  • Proficiency with Xcode, Git, and the Swift language.
  • Experience in developing an application published on the App Store.
  • Experience in developing within code review context (pull request).
  • Knowledge of programming patterns (such as MVC, MVP, or MVVM).
  • Knowledge of SOLID architecture principles is an asset.
  • Ability to read, produce, and adhere to software architecture diagrams (UML, sequence diagram, etc.).
  • Interest in working on an application available on multiple form factors (mobile/tablet/TV).
  • Knowledge of SwiftUI, Combine.
  • Knowledge of AVPlayer, CoreData, and AlamoFire is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Cocoapods (including the design/maintenance of internal pods).
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.

 

Please note this is a 12-month contract position, renewable annually. This regular position is not a consulting assignment but a long-term opportunity with attractive CBC/Radio-Canada employee benefits.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
 

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.

When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.


This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.

 

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in developing complex and high-performance React applications.
  • Proficiency with CSS, SASS, and styled components.
  • Mastery of object-oriented approach in React (OOP).
  • Mastery of JavaScript / TypeScript.
  • Experience with React "hooks» is an asset.
  • Experience with Git.
  • Experience with audio/video players as well as the HLS protocol is an asset.
  • Experience in front-end performance optimization.
  • Experience with Next.js, WebPack and Node.
  • Knowledge of SWR or another data fetching framework.
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.

 

Please note this is a 12-month contract position, renewable annually. This regular position is not a consulting assignment but a long-term opportunity with competitive CBC/Radio-Canada employee benefits.

Your role:


CBC North is looking for a journalist to contribute to the weekly show, Maamuitaau. The job is based at the Montreal office of CBC /Radio-Canada. The journalist will work with a versatile team that is passionate about the language, culture and stories of the James Bay Cree. More specifically, the journalist will conduct interviews in Cree, transcribe recordings, write scripts, process sound and visual footage, and pitch story ideas.  Under the supervision of the show producer, the journalist will produce fact-checked, dynamic, compelling current affairs and news content about the Cree communities to play on various platforms (TV, Digital, radio).


The journalist will present these stories on air and will be trained to follow the Corporation’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.


For reference purposes, and at the time of this posting, the shift is Monday-Friday, 9:00 am-5:00 pm in the office.


Description of duties:


  • Be aware of and understand current events and stakeholders.
  • Be on time (for meetings, delivering scripts, making deadlines etc.)
  • Suggest story ideas/angles, and potential guests.
  • Research and review information, ideas, and audio files
  • Keep up with community contacts and various sources.
  • Recommend and select interviewees. Conduct pre-interviews. Prepare interview questions, approaches and scripts.
  • Conduct interviews in Cree, transcribe recordings, write scripts.
  • Process sound and visual footage
  • Follow up with the team before and during the program. 
  • Suggest intros as needed.
  • Present said stories on air
  • Create and maintain files on upcoming stories.
  • Package content from said interviews for digital platforms
  • Record/edit voice-overs in Dalet
  • Work collaboratively with the team to ensure daily tasks are completed.
  • Carry out all other related tasks as needed.

  • A high school education or an acceptable combination of education and/or
  • experience.
  • Relevant experience appropriate to television, community radio, current affairs or a newsroom
  • environment.

  • In-depth knowledge of current events as they relate to Cree communities, and the people living there.
  • Fluent in the working language (East Cree) and very good knowledge of English.
  • Knowledge of the French language would be considered an asset
  • Knowledge of interview techniques and communications methods specific to TV as well as digital and radio.
  • Interest in honing skills related to digital journalism and open to learning new
  • technology.
  • Strong familiarity with computers and social media
  • Curious and engaging on-air personality and a strong affinity for and interest in the
  • audience.
  • Able to analyze, synthesize and think critically.
  • Able to work under pressure.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

The Opportunity

 

As Junior Consultant (Senior Coordinator), Support - Broadcast Management, you will provide active technical support to users of Radio-Canada broadcast management applications by working alongside dynamic project teams and the Expertise Centre. You will be responsible for analyzing and understanding recurring problems that are part of the business framework.

 

You must analyze and understand the various technical issues experienced by users, contacting them personally as needed. You will work with both developers and teams in Business Technology Solutions teams to resolve more complex issues.

 

You will draft documentation required for troubleshooting and for training first-level support staff.

 

At CBC/Radio-Canada, you’ll find passionate people, challenges and demanding responsibilities that will further your personal and professional growth.

 

What’s in it for you?

 

Challenges. We spend our days solving problems on an unbelievable scale. Media files are highly nuanced and incredibly complicated; updating, installing and supporting technologies that are organization-wide and that impact broadcasting content is a time sensitive, complex technical feat. And that’s just the beginning. Not to mention, you will be working with cutting edge technology in data management, cloud migration, IP for broadcast, AI and security and reliability.

 

As our new Junior Consultant, you will:

  • Analyze, solve and resolve various and complex technological problems.
  • Analyze and evaluate tools and work methodologies in order to make recommendations to optimize them.
  • Develop and implement different tools, processes and optimized work methodology.
  • Implement and coordinate special projects (ex: updating work method for a station).
  • Train support staff and super users.
  • Help advise management in the development of strategic plans.
  • Manage and provide advanced technical support, and maintain systems, applications, equipment and software; ensure that the equipment used works well and is accessible, while ensuring the integrity of the content.
  • Take charge and support regular customers in order to offer high-level technological support (autonomy with decision-making and problem-solving).
  • Establish and sustain communication between the various departments supported and the support teams.
  • Document all changes, optimization or modification in working methods.

 

What You Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a College Diploma in IT support or IT management, or the equivalent.
  • Two (2) years of experience acquired in coordinating a technical team in a user support center.
  • Knowledge of broadcast management applications (OnAir, WO Program, Cognos, Livelink, ScheduAll, RRT, MRO, etc.).
  • Knowledge of the business community in connection with Radio and TV broadcast management systems.
  • Good general knowledge and intellectual curiosity (with respect to acquiring and developing new knowledge and skills).
  • Good analytical sense with an openness to find solutions to problems.
  • Knowledge of or experience with the implementation of Agile principles (Scrum / Kanban) - an asset.
  • Knowledge of or experience with ticket management tools (e.g. Jira, Remedy, etc.) - an asset.
  • Strong analytical skills and openness to find solutions to problems.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, interpersonal skills and client satisfaction.
  • Bilingualism (French and English), spoken and written.
  • Ability to travel within Canada.

CBC Morning Live is looking for an innovative journalist and programmer to create content for live and on-demand audiences, as Producer of Host Content. This is a great opportunity to contribute to CBC News Network, Canada’s top breaking news channel and livestream, and reach new audiences with our world-class content.


In this role, you will work closely with the host of CBC Morning Live on daily and longer-term projects. Working with the senior producer and other program leaders, you identify, develop and produce daily responsive video segments that run within live programming, while ensuring they’re optimized for people to watch on-demand on mobile. You may also produce versions for other platforms, such as text-based digital and audio.


You are deeply versed in a range of news stories, from the trade war to Céline Dion’s return, with a proven ability to create creative treatments that meet audience needs. As such, you produce daily video explainers, breaking down an angle of the top story. You also work on original reporting and newsmaking interviews, often under tight deadlines. You also support breaking news coverage and special programming, including when the program is hosted from the field.  


You have experience writing for broadcast and working with video - from gathering to editing. You know your way around a control room and how a program is crafted. You can also spot opportunities to expand the reach of our journalism to new viewers - always advocating for the audience and how we can address their needs on any given story. You thrive in breaking news and are a fountain of ideas of how to treat it. You thrive in a high-stress, tight-deadline environment and are able to work flexible hours and on weekends, if needed.


The ideal candidate will hit the ground running because of their familiarity with key production tools. Experience on a national news team is crucial and experience working with digital and/or social content is a strong asset.


You will play a leadership role within the team, working closely with colleagues to pitch, produce and focus newsmaking interviews. You will also liaise with other CBC News platforms to plan the rollout of host content and identify coverage opportunities. You live and promote the values of an inclusive and respectful work culture, with strong communication and interpersonal skills. 


This one-year role is based in Toronto and requires full-time, on-site attendance. 


We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • Minimum five (5) years of experience of which three must involve work in a broadcast news environment.
  • Experience pitching stories and translating those ideas into focused on-air segments.
  • Proven original and creative thought in the production of news.
  • Experience directing talent, including field video production.
  • Understanding of audience needs and how audiences consume content across platforms. 
  • Excellent writing, vetting and production skills.
  • Excellent eye and ear for pacing, tone, presentation and production.
  • Thrives in a high pressure breaking news environment with tight deadlines, demonstrating superior news judgement.
  • Experience in a live control room under pressures of a changing lineup or breaking news.
  • A university degree or equivalent.
  • Ability to solve problems quickly, independently and in-group discussions.
  • Demonstrated leadership skills with excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience directing, performing and delegating assignments across editorial, production and technical lines.
  • Ability to perform other producer roles in the newsroom.
  • Experience using Vizrt, iNews and Media Central, and directing editing. 
  • Lives and promotes the values of an inclusive and respectful work culture.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of, and/or connection to underrepresented communities across Canada. 
  • Elevates diverse perspectives, ideas and differing points of view.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience working with CBC Journalistic Standards and Practices.
  • Flexibility to adapt to changing work patterns and methods. Must be available to work evenings, weekend evenings and long days and late nights.

You have skills and interest in leadership and communication, and will have project coordination accountability for components / projects / programs of medium to large complexity and scale.  You are comfortable interacting with delivery groups and other stakeholders at the individual contributor and management levels, to coordinate work, track progress, communicate status, and manage risks and issues.  You have solid project management skills and an understanding of what is involved in projects that involve the acquisition, customization, configuration, validation, integration, and transition of business application or infrastructure systems.  You tailor your approach to the needs, comfortable with traditional, and Agile methodologies to coordinate delivery across multiple streams.

You are adept at understanding the needs of various stakeholders and supporting teams in the initiation and implementation of the group's strategic projects and eager to learn.

 

The Opportunity:

 

As a project coordinator working on the Content Every Day (CED) product family, you will work closely with Agile PMs, Product Owners, Scrum Masters, and the Product Director.  You will ensure coordination across multiple streams, including but not limited to:

  • Financial Coordination:
    • Budget & forecasting: maintain the initiative's financial registry, updating actuals and monthly forecasts, and identifying key variances or trends.
    • Operational finance: execute reconciliation and of timesheets, manage corporate approval workflows to facilitate timely invoice processing.

  • Logistical Coordination: partner with Agile PMs, Scrum Masters, and POs to orchestrate execution of program-level workshops and major planning sessions (schedule alignment, agenda distribution, cross-functional participant coordination).
  • Action & Issue Tracking: Document decisions, track action items, and maintain risk/issue registers across multiple streams, ensuring operational follow-up with responsible owners.

 

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience and training.
  • Five (5) or more years of professional experience including three (3) or more years of professional experience in project management/coordination, business administration, or project support.
  • Bilingual (English/French).
  • Experience with document management, Google Suite, spreadsheet, and presentation packages.
  • Knowledge of / experience with budgeting, financial forecasting and scheduling.
  • Knowledge of traditional, hybrid, and Agile project management methodologies including “Agile at scale” - strong asset.
  • Ability to relate to people representing a range of personalities, cultures and hierarchical levels.
  • Ability to handle working on simultaneous workstreams.

 

Nice to have:

  • Experience with CBC/RC organization.
  • Experience with tools (such as Jira) for tracking sprint progress.
  • Experience using scheduling tools (such as MS Project or roadmap visualization software) for roadmaps and traditional milestones.

Radio-Canada’s News Department is seeking a Project Manager. In this role, you will be responsible for developing staff assignment plans for the Montreal News Centre. You will coordinate all relevant data required to produce these plans (requester needs, reports, spreadsheets, timelines, etc.) efficiently, while ensuring compliance with collective agreements and internal policies.


You will play a strategic planning and advisory role with production teams and senior editorial staff. You will be required to negotiate terms with various stakeholders and find creative solutions to ensure operational continuity, while maintaining compliance with corporate standards and ensuring quality follow-up.


You will be responsible for coordinating information across all relevant departments to establish assignment schedules and secure the necessary approvals to carry out production projects. Your schedule will include on-call shifts worked remotely to address last-minute replacement needs.


The work environment is specific to a newsroom setting, where employees have atypical schedules and each role is distinct. Urgent situations are frequent and stress levels are high; the successful candidate must demonstrate tact, discretion, leadership, and sound judgment when recommending alternative solutions due to changes in plans.


This is primarily a daytime position (both in-office and remote), with additional evening, night, and weekend on-call shifts (remote), shared on a rotating basis with other team members.


Please note that this is a permanent, full-time position.


This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.
