job.title: Conflict Operations Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The International Desk is seeking a Conflict Operations Editor. This is a dedicated newsroom role for a veteran journalist who has demonstrated sharp judgment and leadership working in security-sensitive assignments.  You will help guide our most ambitious and complicated newsgathering efforts, in close partnership with our security team.

You will work closely with the International Editor and the desk’s top leaders to navigate the challenges of reporting in conflict zones and other difficult environments and ensure that the safety and security of our staff is a top priority. You will direct correspondents in the field, serve as a partner to their editors and coordinate with our security advisers and newsroom leadership. You will assess risk and make tough calls while building systems to support our journalists around the world in an era of prolonged and changing war.

This is an in-office position preferably based in London, and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per departmental guidance. You will also be expected to deploy internationally as news events dictate.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and guide newsgathering operations: The primary goal of this position is to inform and ensure we’re making the right calls on assignments in security-sensitive locations.  With guidance and close partnership from our security experts, you will collaborate with senior editors to make the tough decisions on editorial necessity and safety to ensure the safety of our teams in the field. 
  • Leadership Briefings: Provide daily situation and staffing updates for newsroom editors and leadership. Investigate and analyze security incidents and issues to find vulnerabilities and enact corrective measures as needed so we are continuously improving our systems.
  • Establishing Conflict Bureaus: Deploy quickly to rapidly create or scale wartime bureaus. Work with security and the bureau chief to secure and vet critical local infrastructure and ensure our on-the-ground presence and operation supports safety and exceptional journalism.
  • Business continuity: Lead disaster recovery, evacuation planning and crisis management in partnership with our business continuity team.
  • Operational Security : Work in close partnership with the security operation to ensure teams have the specific gear and training required for their assignments, and that we’re following proper protocols to enable our journalists to stay safe while doing their jobs. 
  • Freelancer & Evacuee Support: In collaboration with Legal and Global Operations, coordinate support for our freelancers in conflict zones, and for Times journalists who have had to relocate or evacuate due to conflicts. 
  • Digital Security: Work with our information security team to ensure that journalists in sensitive environments have their data, devices and sources properly protected.
  • Journalistic values: Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

This role reports to the International Editor, based in New York.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Experience working with journalists in conflict zones
  • Experience in a role requiring high-level operational skills and crisis management.
  • Excellent news judgment and understanding of journalistic imperatives.
  • Strong communication skills, able to brief and advise leadership with clarity 
  • Strong collaboration skills, with experience working across a broad range of stakeholders and partners.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Extensive experience in journalism, including significant time as a correspondent or editor in security-sensitive places.
  • Demonstrated experience managing local teams (fixers, drivers, interpreters) in volatile or hostile environments.
  • Demonstrated organizational and process-management skills
  • Willingness to travel internationally, including to security-sensitive locations on short notice.
  • Experience developing safety protocols for complex newsgathering operations

job.description:

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

We are seeking a Marketing Designer to help bring to life the full-funnel creative strategy and execution for our Games subscription offering. This is a hands-on design role for a creative who can translate the value of all we offer — independent journalism and world-class lifestyle products — into clear, compelling campaigns that drive performance and deepen engagement with Games.

Reporting to the Associate Creative Director, Games, Marketing, you will work closely with writers, designers and our audio and video teams, as well as partners in marketing and media strategy, product design, audience insights and brand identity. You'll contribute to integrated campaigns across the full subscriber journey — from full-funnel product launches to subscriber acquisition campaigns to app store optimization efforts and more.

We are looking for a designer who is passionate about both exceptional craft and the collaborative process it takes to create it. You thrive at the intersection of brand and performance, are excited to contribute directly to growth and product marketing initiatives, and partner with more senior creative leaders on the team.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office three days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Contribute to the development and execution of conceptual, visually compelling campaigns and always-on marketing creative for Games, ensuring work supports awareness, consideration, conversion and retention goals.

  • Design and adapt campaign creative across paid, owned and earned channels, including digital, social, email, in-app placements, app stores and OOH, in line with The Times' brand standards.

  • Translate in-product experiences and key feature benefits into clear, marketing assets that deepen engagement and drive habitual product use.

  • Support the in-house adaptation and extension of major brand campaigns, collaborating with creative leaders and agency partners to build cohesive executions across all channels.

  • Help develop and maintain scalable visual systems, templates and libraries that enable rapid testing and iteration while upholding a high bar for design quality and brand consistency.

  • Partner with other designers, art directors, writers and marketers to concept, refine and ship creative that increases subscriptions and engagement with our journalism and products.

  • Work from creative briefs, participate in reviews, and incorporate feedback from stakeholders, staying comfortable with shifts in strategy or approach based on the news cycle or business needs.

  • Assist in creating clear, compelling presentation materials and articulate the rationale behind your design decisions to a broad group of colleagues, including leadership.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Associate Creative Director, Games, Marketing.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of hands-on graphic design experience at an advertising agency, digital agency, studio or in-house team, with a focus on marketing or advertising creative.

  • A design portfolio that shows sharp execution and conceptual thinking across a range of touch points — including social, digital display, email, in-app and print — and demonstrates how your design choices clarify complex ideas for different audiences across the funnel.

  • High proficiency in the formal elements of design, including typography, layout, balance, hierarchy, proportion, color, emphasis and unity, with a refined aesthetic and strong attention to detail from concept through production.

  • Fluency with design and motion tools such as Figma, and Adobe Creative Suite, with files that support iteration, collaboration and production.

  • Hands-on motion and animation experience in After Effects.

  • Comfort working cross-functionally with partners in marketing strategy, media, product design, audience insights and brand identity, and enthusiasm for collaborating on campaigns that not only look great but also perform.

  • Understanding of trends in digital advertising and growth marketing, plus familiarity with the latest social media ecosystem and how brands show up in a way that feels authentic.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A background in subscription, media or content businesses, with familiarity in how brand, product marketing, and performance media work together across the funnel.

  • Experience working in video editing software and a working knowledge of on set video production for social channels.

Wirecutter is looking for a strategic and operationally oriented partnerships leader who is passionate about driving performance-based results that provide the best buying experience on Wirecutter Picks. The Director, Commerce Partnerships reports directly to the Executive Director, Commerce and is the team leader responsible for business development, partnerships and affiliate operations.  You will emphasize building career development plans through active mentorship of the team, and working across the organization to achieve our goals and priorities. This role is open to remote hiring. This is a temporary role running from September 2026 - May 2027.

  • Oversee the strategic development of Wirecutter’s affiliate revenue growth strategies to meet EPC targets and diversification goals, and manages important strategic partners.

  • Partner with Data Insights, Product, and Editorial leadership to identify and implement action plans against headwinds and growth opportunities.
  • You serve as the strategic and operational partner to the Deputy Editors around coverage of tentpole moments and sale events.
  • You will foster Wirecutter’s relationships across agencies and networks and further our status as the gold standard in commerce content.
  • You will partner with the Executive Director to implement career development plans and mentor direct reports to develop and retain a high-performance team.
  • Attend affiliate conferences throughout the year.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of professional experience with an emphasis on client services, business development and/or partnerships.
  • 4+ years experience in a business facing affiliate marketing role is required.
  • A track record for growing revenue targets and implementing new revenue strategies valued at a minimum of 8 figures, with experience in financial management e.g. forecasting against goals and budgets, revenue growth, and profitability.

  • Strong relationships with merchant, agency, and network partners in the affiliate space.
  • Proficient knowledge of attribution models and tracking methodologies across device types and the major affiliate networks.
  • Experience communicating with and presenting to senior executives, and translating company priorities into actionable goals for teams.

The New York Times is looking for a Director, HR Business Partner for the Product Engineering and Technology groups to support and partner with the Chief Technology Officer, leaders, managers and employees across the technology function, and with our Chief Product Officer. You will manage a team of two, while also supporting employees directly. You will report to the VP, HR Business Partners.

The Director, HRBP plays a critical role in driving a people strategy aligned with enterprise goals. You will be the primary HR partner to support our Chief Technology Officer (CTO), Chief Product Officer (CPO), managers, and employees of the technology organization - including guidance, management of the performance enablement cycle, and oversight of process/HR administration.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office 3+ days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Be an advisor, partner, and coach to senior leaders, managers, and individual contributors across our Technology group, including the Chief Technology Officer and Chief Product Officer
  • Lead and develop a team of two HR Business Partners to manage multiple HR issues and support the business
  • Provide daily support to senior-level department leaders, managers, and employees, providing coaching, management of employee lifecycles and performance management, and oversight of process/HR administration
  • Lead planning, communication support and implementation of company and department-level people initiatives, developing programs and solutions to meet department needs
  • Partner with Centers of Excellence (COEs) to deliver impactful people initiatives to client groups. Provide COEs with clear, relevant feedback on how to refine and enhance people initiatives over time
  • Partner with leadership to monitor how business plans and industry trends may affect talent needs, HR priorities, and the way your client groups are organized or operate
  • Partner with business leaders on setting priorities and monitoring progress to create an inclusive workplace for all employees
  • Develop and interpret relevant people metrics to identify trends and provide insights that shape HR strategy and talent recommendations, and lead cross-functional initiatives
  • Collaborate with Employee Relations, Talent Management, and Legal teams to investigate and resolve employee relations issues, ensure regulatory compliance, and identify development needs for employees
  • Handle daily operational tasks, such as answering requests and inquiries from employees, and assisting with HRIS transactions
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • 10+ years of increasing HR Business Partner experience and responsibility with experience managing a range of HR disciplines, including employee relations, employment law, labor relations, talent management and development, compensation, and inclusion within technology or adjacent teams
  • 5+ years of experience leading people, with a focus on developing a motivated, engaged, and inclusive team
  • Experience working with an HRIS, e.g., Workday, SuccessFactors

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent in HR, business, psychology, or relevant field preferred - SPHR, CIPD, or equivalent professional accreditation
  • Experience working in a matrix of functional and geographic teams in public companies, media, or includes aspects of employee relations
  • Experience providing research/data backed ideas to create a successful employee experience that is rooted in an equitable and inclusive culture

job.title: Editor at Large, Opinion, A.I.
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Opinion department is seeking a sophisticated editorial leader to spearhead our coverage of one of the most consequential shifts of our time: the rise of artificial intelligence. This role is designed for an editor with a deep background in intellectual history, policy and narrative journalism — someone capable of moving beyond the daily news cycle to deliver definitive enterprise work that explains how AI is reshaping society, labor and the human experience.

The ideal candidate will combine the intellectual rigor of a long-form editor with the tactical agility required to edit and manage high-profile columnists and drive a department-wide coverage strategy.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and coordinate Opinion's cross-platform strategy for AI coverage, identifying the most urgent moral, political and economic questions raised by emerging technologies
  • Commission and edit ambitious enterprise projects, deep-dive features and essays that provide historical context and forward-looking analysis of the AI revolution
  • Collaborate with graphics, multimedia and audience teams to create innovative digital presentations for complex technical and philosophical topics
  • Manage and edit a portfolio of New York Times columnists and contributing writers, providing high-touch guidance on narrative voice, structural clarity and argumentative rigor
  • Identify and recruit guest essayists and new recurring voices who can contribute specialized expertise on technology, ethics and the future
  • Manage a team of writers to refine their perspectives, ensuring that every piece of commentary meets the highest standards of intellectual honesty and literary excellence
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Opinion Editorial Director.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience in senior editorial roles at a major national publication
  • A proven track record of editing complex, ideas-driven journalism and high-profile writers
  • Exceptional ability to synthesize technical information into compelling, accessible narratives for a general audience
  • A deep interest in the intersection of technology and public policy, with an established network of thinkers and practitioners in the AI space
  • Experience managing large-scale editorial projects from conception through publication
  • Sophisticated understanding of the digital media landscape and a commitment to maintaining The Times's standards of editorial excellence

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience collaborating with data journalists and visual editors to build interactive or data-driven explainers that make abstract AI concepts tangible for a general audience
  • A track record of developing the next generation of editors and writers, fostering a culture of intellectual curiosity and rigorous fact-checking

The New York Times is looking for an experienced, imaginative senior editor to lead Wesley Morris's weekly culture show, Cannonball, which debuted in 2025. This role is fundamentally about partnership: working closely with one of the great cultural critics of our time to keep developing the show and reaching new heights; and leading a small team of producers to translate Wesley's critical voice, instincts, and curiosity into a show that feels as engaging as it is intellectually sharp.

The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work.

This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. You are an experienced and accomplished culture editor/writer/producer/thinker in your own right, someone with ideas about what's going on in the world of movies, TV, books, music, art and more. You have a keen sense of who the interesting critical voices in this landscape are, and a sense of how to program great guests each week. You are well-organized, someone capable of leading a multidisciplinary team through the many overlapping stages of development and production on multiple episodes at a time. You're adept at working within a larger editorial system, taking notes and other input. You have an understanding of YouTube and other social platforms where the show may travel. You have a feel for the right way to use audience data to inform editorial decision-making. You're adaptable, friendly, creative, and discerning. And above all, you're interested in and capable of doing all the work—both the glamorous and exciting stuff and the basic but necessary stuff—to build a successful show.

As senior editor of Cannonball, you will also be part of the staff of The New York Times Magazine, where Wesley is a staff writer and where the show is based. You will draw on and be part of the magazine's cultural coverage.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as an editorial partner to Wesley Morris, shaping episode ideas, refining arguments, and helping translate his voice and sensibility into a compelling episode.
  • Come up with interesting ideas for guests and manage the process of bringing them in and staging successful conversations with Wesley.
  • Lead the editorial process from pitch through final cut, including story development, scripting, structural editing, and post-production feedback.
  • Collaborate with producers, editors, and Magazine and Shows leadership to ensure editorial clarity, creative ambition, and high production quality across every episode.
  • Manage and mentor a multidisciplinary team, setting clear expectations, providing feedback, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing culture.
  • Oversee production timelines and workflows, ensuring deadlines are met without compromising quality or ambition.
  • Maintain a strong, consistent editorial voice while pushing the show to expand creatively and reach new audiences.
  • Develop new formats and concepts for a show that's still evolving.
  • Work with Magazine leadership to integrate the show into the Magazine's editorial plans, voice and design, helping the show grow into a recurring, high‑impact Magazine franchise.
  • Partner with audience, analytics, and platform teams to understand viewer and listener behavior and refine the show's format, distribution, and growth strategy.
  • Work cross-functionally with other newsroom desks and teams to identify opportunities for collaboration, guest booking, and editorial alignment.
  • Work proactively with Legal and Standards departments to keep the show free of corrections and/or legal challenges.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Magazine's Deputy Editor overseeing Culture.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience editing/producing cultural coverage—criticism, cultural reporting, and storytelling in a variety of formats.
  • 5+ years experience in audio and/or video production and editing, including managing soup‑to‑nuts production of long‑form, conversational shows.
  • Deep interest in movies, TV, books, music, art, and all forms of culture (both rarefied/literary and pop).
  • Sophisticated sense of how criticism can work to open up, explore and define a work of art by reading it closely, putting it in larger context, and registering a personal response to it.
  • Sharp instincts for the ways that ideas about culture intersect with everything else: politics, history, technology, identity, business, and everyday life.
  • Familiarity with digital storytelling formats.
  • Experience working with talent.
  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing — from structuring episodes and pacing to line editing and shaping host conversations to guiding group edits and editorial brainstorms.
  • Belief in The New York Times's mission and a strong commitment to journalistic independence, fairness and accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience with a weekly publishing cadence and in managing teams under deadline.
  • 5+ years experience managing teams, including setting expectations, giving feedback and supporting people's growth.
  • Proven ability to foster an inclusive, diverse and innovative environment, both on‑air and within the team.
  • Deep familiarity with vertical video platforms and the changing social media landscape.
  • Knowledge of YouTube and social video strategy, or a demonstrated ability to learn and apply platform best practices in partnership with audience and video colleagues.
  • Experience in Adobe Premiere.

job.title: Graphics Multimedia Editor, Open-source Reporting
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Graphics team is looking for a reporter with extensive open-source and investigative reporting skills to turn raw evidence into impactful visual stories. You have a track record for uncovering exclusive information off the news.

The Graphics team is a leader in using spatial and visual techniques on investigative stories, and we're looking for someone who is passionate about accountability journalism using cutting-edge reporting techniques.

Below are a few examples of the kinds of stories that you will be a part of:
  • An exclusive look at the failed columns of the Midtown Manhattan near-collapse
  • A 3-D analysis of why firefighters' lines of sight were limited in the deadly LaGuardia Crash
  • An investigation into the mass graves in Syria
  • An investigation into the causes of a Miami building collapse
  • A spatial investigation into a deadly fire in the Bronx
  • A forensic analysis of an apartment building collapse in the Turkey earthquake
Working with journalists on the Graphics team and across the newsroom, you will play an important role in shaping visual reconstructions and investigations that rely on spatial analysis or use 3-D modeling. You will gather and analyze evidence for stories across a wide range of topics for both quick-turn stories as well as longer-term enterprise.

You will be expected to take the initiative in leading major storylines, with the goal of uncovering new or exclusive findings across multiple visual story formats. You should be curious and driven, and be comfortable with moving between solo deep dives and fast-paced, cross-desk collaborations.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days a week.

Responsibilities:
  • Bring core OSINT fluency to the desk's coverage: geolocation, chronolocation, satellite/aerial imagery analysis, audio-video research, and more.
  • Analyze a variety of data sources, including satellite and aerial imagery, flight/vessel tracking data, social media platforms and radio scanner data.
  • Vet and build relationships with a network of sources on stories.
  • Generate ideas that help the team develop custom tooling to automate open-source reporting for analyzing and visualizing evidence.
  • Find new ways to report beyond the standard OSINT toolkit, by using computational techniques, including through machine learning, computer vision and approved AI tools.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to an Assistant Editor on the Graphics desk.
Basic Qualifications:
  • 5+ years of relevant experience as an investigative reporter, open-source researcher or forensic expert.
  • Proven experience conducting open-source investigations by sourcing audio and visual evidence across a variety of platforms.
  • Experience producing accountability journalism, with a strong portfolio.
  • Experience producing clear copy about the visual evidence on tight deadlines.
  • Experience verifying user-generated content from social media for authenticity.
  • Skilled in building timelines using a variety of sources, including official statements and metadata from user-generated content.
  • Familiarity with open-source intelligence tools and techniques like Google Earth, satellite imagery platforms, scanner audio data, flight or vessel tracking, or similar.
Preferred Qualifications:
  • Experience working both independently and collaboratively while managing multiple research threads.
  • Experience with advanced tools for reporting, such as QGIS, Blender for 3-D scene reconstructions, data analysis methods, audio and image forensics tools.
  • Adept at creating clear, visual explainers piecing together complex findings.
  • Familiarity with programming and custom tool development.
  • Familiarity with Adobe Suite and Figma.
  • Experience with web scraping tools and working with APIs.
  • Experience using command line tools.
  • Willingness and flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed.

The HRIS Analyst II reports directly to the HRIS Senior Manager and is important for optimizing and supporting Workday Performance, Core HCM, Compensation, HR reporting, and related areas. Primary responsibilities include system configuration, issue troubleshooting, data analysis, testing, production support, and creating mid-level reports. Working with senior HRIS analysts, the HR operations team, and partners, you will guide enhancements to provide HR technology solutions.

This is a hybrid role based in our Norfolk, VA office. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Be a primary technical contact for the Workday Performance module, while providing functional support for Core HCM, Compensation, Payroll, and Time/Absence domains.

  • Accomplish end-to-end system configuration to support global performance evaluation cycles.

  • Be a primary contact for performance workflow design and resolution of technical issues.

  • Deliver technical and user support for Workday, handling questions, troubleshooting, and resolving issues across supported modules.

  • Execute assigned production support tickets and project tasks with high accuracy and within target deadlines.

  • Maintain HCM production support processes, encompassing monitoring, detailed analysis, and issue resolution.

  • Define, refine, and maintain business process configurations.

  • Configure, schedule, and oversee automated mass actions and system alert notifications.

  • Participate in Workday's biannual feature update cycles.

  • Collaborate with the Workday Security team to configure and maintain domain and business process security policies.

  • Design and deploy Workday solutions tailored to meet functional requirements and improve operational efficiency.

  • Test, and implement new feature enhancements, analyzing impacts across Performance, Compensation, HCM, Benefits, Payroll, reporting, and integrations.

  • Audit and validate system data and reports to preserve data integrity and maintain internal control standards.

  • Review end-user data entry practices to identify process gaps and strengthen data governance controls.

  • Provide HRIS system maintenance, solution implementations, and module troubleshooting.

  • Partner with senior HRIS analysts to achieve shared goals, exchange technical knowledge, and foster skill growth.

  • Engage with HR partners to lead new module functionality, enhancements, and broader HCM programs.

  • Communicate technical insights, analytical findings to non-technical partners.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • Minimum 2 years of experience in an HRIS Analyst or functional HR systems role.

  • Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience configuring and maintaining Workday Performance Management.

  • Demonstrated experience writing and generating custom Workday reports.

  • Experience maintaining Workday business processes, security protocols, and system release updates.

  • Advanced proficiency in Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel (e.g., complex formulas, pivot tables).

job.title: Newsroom Operations Manager
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Role

The New York Times is looking for an operational owner and highly organized self-starter to join our Newsroom Operations team as an Operations Manager. You will provide hands-on support and oversight of numerous logistics involved in the smooth daily operation of several assigned department(s) – News Platforms and Data, T Magazine and others.

We are looking for a quick learner and creative problem solver who is capable of handling the ever-changing demands of a fast-paced newsroom environment. You will guide tasks across the finish line for the desks in the newsroom. Key to this will be supporting members of our masthead and our journalists with a variety of daily responsibilities and short- and long-term projects. This includes being at the center of on-the-ground coordination of both in-office and offsite events, ensuring execution of on-site logistics and meals for key news coverage events, ensuring that administrative operational tasks are completed by internal deadlines so that operations on the desk run continually and uninterrupted. You will report directly to a Senior Manager of Newsroom Operations.

This role will be Hybrid, with a required in-office presence of 4 days a week. The schedule of these 4 days can fluctuate based on the needs of the desks, and during some peak news cycles, you may be required to be on site for 5 days during those weeks.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the primary, accountable operational contact for members of the masthead, department heads, and journalists, resolving operational roadblocks independently.
  • Responsible for on-site setup of various in-office events including mock elections, team all hands gatherings of staff from around the country, team lunches and various similar events, and also serving as a production coordinator for all such events. including live coverage setups, catering logistics, seating arrangements, and equipment deployment during breaking news cycles.
  • Oversee complex equipment setups for assigned desks, special coverage teams, and events, ensuring that all hardware, workstation, and specialized technical configurations in real-time to ensure journalists have fully functioning tools.
  • Work with the Newsroom Finance team to help create annual budgets and provide oversight of those budgets, including monthly closes, supplying additional financial reports.
  • Manage work and vacation schedules and maintain accurate time banks in Workday, and work with Payroll to verify time banks for transfers, departures, and annual payouts.
  • Manage a travel calendar and be sure anyone traveling on assignment is properly set up on the company's business travel accident insurance.
  • Approve expenses and travel costs in Workday.
  • Manage and process freelancers and vendors' payments, working with the Contracts Manager
  • Oversee accounts payable and accounts receivable for assigned departments
  • Work with HR and recruiting teams to assist with position management transactions
  • Facilitate Workday management, including onboarding new employees and helping them to get the training, equipment, and information they need
  • Keep staffing lists, org charts, and various email distribution lists up to date with any staffing changes in the department
  • Purchase supplies and equipment, keep track of all departmental expenses, including capital spending and outside vendor spending
  • Work in Zip for independent contractor onboarding, sourcing events and purchasing
  • Be available for a variety of tasks that come up, often urgently, including troubleshooting, assisting writers and editors,with on-site and off-site needs, etc.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in an operational or administrative role
  • Ability to drive projects forward
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Experience dealing with detailed and confidential and private concerns
  • You can work and keep an optimistic attitude while maintaining a keen sense of urgency
  • Be accessible after hours or on weekends when circumstances require
  • Impeccable organizational and time management skills; ability to multitask, prioritize and work under deadline pressure
  • Ability to work with all levels of management and staff and manage the needs of a team of 100+ employees and leaders

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of training and experience
  • Able to research resources, troubleshoot, and solve problems
  • Workday experience

job.title: Research Director, Audience Insights, Content Insights
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Research Director, Content Insights will have a critical role informing the creation, iteration and measurement of video and video products at the New York Times. You will lead all video measurement research to inform our understanding of how video content performs across platforms, surfaces, and audience segments. You will oversee the end-to-end measurement of video effectiveness, from individual videos to longer-form recurring concepts, and translate data into relevant strategies that inform production, distribution, and editorial decisions. You will also work with product, design, and editorial teams to improve on-platform video experiences.

You will report to the Managing Director, News Products on the Audience Insights Team and will collaborate with partners across the Newsroom. You understand how to blend market research and user research methods and practices into actionable insights for an entire mission.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop audience research to support the creation and growth of video franchises and recurring shows. Drawing on research methods used by production studios and streaming networks, you'll conduct research that can inform greenlight decisions — including concept testing, pilot testing, audience appetite studies, and competitive landscape analysis.
  • Partner with video leadership to evaluate whether a format, host, or editorial premise has the demand to sustain an audience over time. For existing shows, help build longitudinal tracking that monitors audience health: loyalty, satisfaction, and reasons for churn.
  • Help build a video performance tracking program grounded in survey-based measurement, tracking metrics like awareness, recall, engagement, and sentiment among defined audience segments over time.
  • Working alongside analytics teams, you'll help establish benchmarks, monitor performance across all surfaces where video is published (owned and operated, social, streaming), and develop a consistent cadence of reporting that gives editorial, product, and business stakeholders a reliable read on how our videos are landing with audiences.
  • Lead quantitative and qualitative research among target audiences to support video strategy and format development (e.g., format preference studies, thumbnail and title concept tests, viewer satisfaction studies). Partner with video producers and editors to understand their needs and scope appropriate methodologies, from brief development through questionnaire design, survey launch, and insight delivery.
  • Manage multiple research projects and ad-hoc requests simultaneously, developing timelines and planning resources.
  • Partner or lead research on other editorial projects and franchises, such as newsletters, podcasts, or other emerging products
  • Collaborate with research partners, analytics teams, and company partners.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the quality, speed, and effect of video measurement, including recommending new vendors, tools, and methodologies.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in market research, user research, or consumer insights, with an emphasis on multimodal and product research.
  • Proficiency in both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies and experience with continuous improvement and new ideas.
  • Experience leading all facets of a tracking program, including vendor relationships, questionnaire development, data mining, and reporting.
  • Fluency in analyzing large datasets, identifying insights, and creating clear reports.
  • Experience developing timelines across multiple projects, applying project management skills.
  • Experience managing external research partners/vendors.
  • Experience with visualization tools and creating compelling presentations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • B.A./B.S. degree.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. The New York Times is an industry leader in visual journalism with reporting that includes extraordinary news coverage, investigations, culture and lifestyle reporting. The Reporter Video team identifies compelling stories and brings the depth and breadth of our news report onto our site and other platforms through video that features the expertise of our world-class journalists.

We are looking for an experienced video editor with a portfolio that demonstrates the ability to deliver engaging work on tight deadlines. You will work across a range of newsroom video coverage focused on vertical video storytelling with The Times' world-class journalists on-camera. You have deep experience in breaking and ongoing news coverage, with a track record of creating digitally compelling short-form video journalism.

Your portfolio and work samples should reveal a strong grasp of modern mobile video storytelling, and it should show that you're a quick learner with creative ideas and the ability to work on small or large teams. You are collaborative and solid technically with a solutions mindset, detail oriented, organized and fast.

Please note we have two positions available in the newsroom. Please speak to your expertise and/or interest(s) in your cover letter:

  • News and Enterprise

  • Culture and Lifestyle (music and film to fashion and real estate)

These are in-office positions based in New York and include regular attendance in the office four days each week. We are open to a Senior Video Editor working out of our LA office for the News and Enterprise role only. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Video editing and color correction of news, culture, enterprise and investigative videos featuring reporters from across the newsroom.

  • Collaborate with video journalists and producers in the pre/post production process, including writing, structure and creative execution. Demonstrate excellent news judgment across projects.

  • Deliver top-notch product under intense deadline pressure, and without the need for direct supervision, continuous editorial guidance, or task management.

  • Work across a range of stories with various newsroom desks including culture and styles, often juggling multiple projects.

  • Work with animators to incorporate animation, motion graphics and house design styles into videos.

  • Experiment with different formats of vertical and mobile visual storytelling.

  • Guide junior staff on edits as needed.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to a Senior Producer based in New York.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of multimedia storytelling, video editing and production experience at a major news video outlet and/or production company. (Minimum 5 years of video editing experience.)

  • Strong digital video editing background.

  • Expertise in Adobe Premiere and Creative Suite.

  • Strong audio editing, mixing and fixing skills for video.

  • Proven ability to craft stories, own video research for a project and edit a video with oversight from managers and senior staff.

  • Thorough knowledge of current events, with experience covering news.

  • The ability to conceive and create fresh original videos related to the news.

  • Must have an impressive portfolio of video editing primarily for digital or broadcast.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience animating and editing animations in Adobe After Effects.

  • A digital first mindset to editing on-platform and for social media.

  • Familiarity with the latest video editing techniques and technologies.

  • The ability to make quick decisions under intense deadlines in a high-pressure newsroom setting.

  • A foundational knowledge of legal, ethical, copyright and usage issues for visuals.

  • Well-versed in the world of social and digital media, with a keen eye on what competitors are doing and what new tools are being used.

job.title: Technical Product Manager II, Content Metadata
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Publishing group at the New York Times is responsible for the content management system for all of the Times: one that empowers development teams to build and evolve innovative experiences with speed and agility, and one that empowers editors and creators with a unified and interconnected suite of tools they can use with confidence to make the world's best journalism.

The Content Data Products Team at the New York Times is responsible for building and governing centralized, flexible platforms that serve as the definitive, compliance-cleared source for our content data. As the media landscape evolves, ensuring that our rich archive of journalism is seamlessly structured, fully attributed, and ready for next-generation platforms is a core priority. We are seeking a curious, collaborative, and analytical Technical Product Manager II to lead strategy and development for content metadata, focusing on attribution, taxonomy, and the development of a knowledge graph.

Content metadata plays a foundational role in The Times' AI strategy. As a Technical Product Manager II, you will own a vision for metadata systems that takes into account editorial needs and objectives, the requirements of our AI Platforms and Products group, Partnerships, differences across Times brands (News, Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic, and Games) and multimedia content types, and the requirements of our journalistic mission. You'll provide strategic direction for and oversee the execution of a product roadmap, leading a team of engineers. You'll report to the Senior Technical Product Manager, Content Data Products.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Own and drive the product strategy and roadmap for content metadata and taxonomy, including foundational work towards the development of a knowledge graph.
  • Partner with operations, legal, and cross-functional teams to map archival data structures, systematically identifying and addressing metadata gaps to improve the depth of our content catalog.
  • Collaborate with engineering, design, editorial/taxonomy teams, and the AI Platforms & Products mission to gather requirements & prioritize features.
  • Communicate product vision, strategy, and progress to partners and stakeholders.
  • Lead the product development lifecycle from conception to launch, ensuring timely delivery and high-quality results.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3–5 years of experience in technical product management, metadata architecture, digital asset management/content management systems, or enterprise information systems.
  • Proven track record of successfully launching and managing complex software products.
  • Experience communicating complex technical concepts to a variety of audiences.
  • 3+ years of experience working with engineering teams
  • Understanding of SQL and an intuitive grasp of relational database architecture. Must be comfortable diving into database schemas to audit and understand data structure.
  • A proven track record of entering ambiguous cross-functional spaces, conducting independent research, interviewing diverse stakeholders, and defining technical requirements.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A degree in Computer Science, Data Science, or Library/Information Science with a focus on Information Architecture or Taxonomy.
  • Proven experience managing data classification, complex metadata models, or combining disparate datasets across multiple systems.
  • Familiarity with knowledge graphs, semantic web concepts, or an active curiosity about how structured metadata powers modern search engines and AI features.
  • Experience working in an Agile environment

job.title: Temporary Social Media Editor, NYT Cooking
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

New York Times Cooking is looking for a temporary social media editor with strong writing skills, sharp strategic instincts, an eye for visuals and a love of food to join our interdisciplinary, fast-growing team through the end of the year.

In this role, you'll be responsible day to day for our Facebook account, building and publishing a high volume of engaging feed posts and video content. You'll pair food photography and video with sharp, compelling copy that inspires people to cook and ultimately drives them to NYT Cooking on platform.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Build, schedule and publish a high volume of daily content on Facebook.
  • Write sharp, engaging captions and on-screen text. Workshop headlines and copy with editors to ensure everything published reflects the smart, accessible and entertaining voice of NYT Cooking.
  • Select, crop, and optimize food photography for Facebook feeds. Add text, graphics and layout elements to posts using design platforms like Figma.
  • Publish daily vertical videos on Facebook Reels to drive reach, engagements and referrals.
  • Foster community by actively engaging with our followers in Facebook comments; translate conversations happening on Facebook into actionable, relevant content and product ideas.
  • Actively participate in regular Facebook promo meetings, brainstorming creative ways to visually package and promote upcoming recipes, articles, videos and seasonal tentpoles.
  • Work towards traffic and engagement goals on our Facebook account; use analytics to make informed decisions that serve the Cooking strategy. Interpret data and signals to know what content is the right fit for what audiences at what time (holidays, seasonality, trends).
  • Track engagement rates, growth statistics, reader responses and other metrics. Regularly communicate these data points to the editorial team, translating them into actionable takeaways that shape future storytelling.
  • Collaborate with social editors of other NYT Facebook accounts, finding opportunities to reach new audiences and drive traffic back to site.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Assistant Editor, NYT Cooking.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience working as a social editor or manager for a brand or publication, with direct experience running high-follower Facebook accounts.
  • Exceptional editorial judgement and copywriting skills, with the ability to write clearly, concisely, and in a distinct, engaging voice.
  • Hands-on experience with social scheduling platforms, graphic design platforms like Figma, database platforms like AirTable and digital analytics software like Facebook Insights, Dash Social, ManyChat, NewsWhip and Google Analytics.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A strategic mind with a bend towards testing and iterating to find what resonates with various audiences.
  • Functional cooking knowledge or culinary experience, and a love of cooking and recipes.
  • A commitment to collaboration and collegiality.
  • Willingness to learn new skills and pitch in when needed to accomplish the goals of a small team.
  • A deep passion for food, cooking and the mission of The New York Times.

job.title: Video Journalist, Reporter Video
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is an industry leader in visual journalism with reporting that includes extraordinary news coverage, investigations, and culture and lifestyle reporting. The Reporter Video team identifies compelling stories and brings the depth and breadth of our news report onto our site and other platforms through video that features the expertise of our world-class journalists.

This is a role for someone who wants to produce, edit and publish short-form vertical videos daily and is versatile enough to work on news, features, enterprise and investigative projects with colleagues across the newsroom. You have expertise in video storytelling, including video editing and writing for narration and social copy, as well as a sharp sense of the digital landscape.

Your portfolio and work samples should reveal a strong grasp of modern mobile video storytelling, and it should show that you're a quick learner with creative ideas and the ability to work on small or large teams. You are solid technically, ideas-oriented and have solid news judgment. Cinematography skills are an added asset. We're looking for someone who excels on deadlines and has experience juggling multiple projects at any given time.

Please note we have three positions in the newsroom. Please speak to your expertise and/or interest(s) in your cover letter:

  • General news

  • Investigations

  • Enterprise

These are in-office positions based in New York and include regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Write, produce, edit and publish short-form vertical videos every day.

  • Help to identify breaking news and enterprise across our news report and create video that features the expertise of our journalists, whether working with reporters on camera or using voiceover or visual storytelling techniques including graphics and animation.

  • Write scripts, wordsmith text and copy edit.

  • Experiment with various forms of short-form vertical video storytelling.

  • Collaborate with visual editors to generate video formats that bring our best journalism to new audiences.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to a Senior Producer.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of video storytelling, video editing and production experience at a news organization.

  • Excellent news judgment and proven ability to work with colleagues and reporters to synthesize newsgathering and/or investigations into a tight, informative and engaging video.

  • Experience producing shoots and interviewing experts on camera.

  • Experience creating original videos that intelligently incorporate audio, video, still images and text.

  • Strong video editing skills with Adobe Premiere.

  • Facility in using photo, video, audio, graphics and animation in storytelling.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Able to meet deadlines and adapt to change within an unpredictable news and production environment.

  • Design and animation skills including experience with design and animation software (Figma, Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects).

  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.

  • Available to work a flexible schedule.

job.title: Account Executive
job.description:
Account Executive 

*Non-Remote, In-Person Opportunity. * 

 

The Opportunity: 

Townsquare Media is looking for a bright, confident, driven individual to join our multimedia advertising sales team in Bozeman Montana.  Townsquare Media Bozeman is an industry leader in digital advertising and an accredited marketing partner of both Google and Meta as well as home to five top radio stations.   

 

At Townsquare Media Bozeman, we are a team of ambitious individuals who work together to push ourselves and those around us to grow personally and professionally. You can expect a dynamic and competitive work environment that fosters success, training, development, and an unlimited earning potential! 

 

If you’re ready to embark upon an exciting career that affords you the opportunity to form meaningful client relationships, develop creative advertising campaigns using our best-in-class multimedia solutions, all while having your finger on the pulse of Southwest Montana…then we want to hear from you!  

 

What You’ll Do: 

  • Identify, pursue, and schedule meetings with local business owners and decision makers to discuss and uncover their marketing needs and challenges 
  • Use our proprietary data, analytics, and multimedia marketing solutions to build, present, and sell customized advertising plans to potential clients  
  • Build, maintain and develop close working relationships with your clients to identify and upsell new advertising solutions 
  • Use your influence and relationship-building skills to provide ongoing customer service, research, and market analysis 
  • You will be responsible for bringing our premier marketing and advertising solutions to local and regional businesses in the Bozeman area and beyond 
  • You will work with and sell integrated advertising solutions including broadcast radio, LIVE event sponsorships and digital including website design, SEO, SEM, Programmatic, Social, Streaming TV and much more 

 

What You’ll Bring: 

  • 1+ year of sales or marketing experience (preferred) 
  • Strong marketing and advertising acumen 
  • Effective verbal and written communications are essential 
  • Experience selling or a working knowledge of digital advertising solutions preferred 
  • Goal-oriented, strong work ethic and a desire to learn and grow a career in Sales 
  • A passion towards customer focused solution sales 
  • Valid driver's license, auto insurance, and vehicle (required) 
  • BA/BS degree (preferred) 

 

What’s In It for You? 

  • Competitive compensation package with UNCAPPED earning potential  
  • 3 weeks PTO + 9 paid holidays (including 2 personal days) 
  • Volunteer Time Off—give back to your community 
  • Health, Dental, Vision, and Pet Insurance 
  • 401(k) with company match + Employee Stock Purchase Plan 
  • Company-provided laptop 
  • Casual, high-energy, supportive, and collaborative work environment 
  • 4-week long sales training program  
  • Unlimited growth opportunities!  

 

Why Townsquare Media Group? 

Townsquare is a community-focused digital media, digital marketing solutions, and radio company focused outside the Top 50 markets in the U.S. Our assets include Townsquare Interactive, a digital marketing services subscription business providing websites, search engine optimization, social platforms, and online reputation management for approximately 21,900 SMBs; Townsquare IGNITE, a proprietary digital programmatic advertising technology with an in-house demand and data management platform; and Townsquare Media, our portfolio of 357 local radio stations in 74 cities with corresponding local news and entertainment websites and apps along with a network of national music/content brands.

job.title: Business Development Representative
job.description:
Business Development Representative

*This is a full-time, in-office opportunity. *

 

This Isn't Another Sales Job. It's Your Chance to Build Something Bigger.

Let's be honest—there are thousands of sales jobs.
Most ask you to sell one product. Make cold calls. Hit a quota. Repeat.
This isn't one of them.

At Townsquare Media Grand Rapids, you'll help shape the success of local businesses while representing some of the most recognized brands in West Michigan. You'll have the backing of a company that combines the power of market-leading radio stations, streaming audio, live events, streaming TV, websites, social media, search marketing, programmatic advertising, SEO, websites, and cutting-edge digital solutions—all under one roof.

Every day is different. Every client is different. Every success story is yours to create.

If you're energized by competition, love solving business challenges, and want unlimited earning potential while working alongside an exceptional team, we'd love to meet you.

 

Why Townsquare Media Group?

Townsquare Media is one of America's largest and most innovative local media companies, operating 354 radio stations and more than 400 local websites across 74 markets nationwide.

In Grand Rapids, we're more than a media company—we're woven into the fabric of the community. Our brands entertain, inform, and connect hundreds of thousands of people every week while helping businesses grow through powerful, measurable marketing solutions.

Our clients don't hire us to buy advertising.
They partner with us to grow their businesses.
That's where you come in.

 

What You’ll Do:

You'll become a trusted marketing advisor to local business owners and decision-makers, helping them navigate today's rapidly evolving media landscape.
You'll work with entrepreneurs, CEOs, marketing directors, nonprofits, and community leaders to develop customized marketing strategies that deliver real business results.

Every day you'll:

  • Build new relationships with businesses throughout West Michigan
  • Create strategic marketing plans using radio, streaming audio, streaming TV, websites, social media, SEO, search marketing, programmatic advertising, events, and more
  • Present creative ideas that help clients grow revenue and strengthen their brands
  • Negotiate and close new business
  • Collaborate with creative, digital, programming, and leadership teams to bring campaigns to life
  • Become a respected business resource within the community

No two days look alike—and that's exactly what makes this role exciting.

 

Who Thrives Here?

Our best Account Executives are naturally curious, highly competitive, resilient, and genuinely enjoy helping people succeed.
They don't see themselves as salespeople.
They see themselves as consultants, entrepreneurs, and problem-solvers.

You'll be a great fit if you:

  • Love building relationships
  • Enjoy winning new business
  • Are energized by goals and competition
  • Take pride in delivering exceptional client service
  • Want to continue learning in one of the fastest-changing industries in business
  • Believe your income should reflect your performance

 

What You’ll Bring:

  • 2+ years of experience in sales (required)
  • Consistent record of meeting or exceeding sales goals
  • Confidence prospecting and developing new business opportunities
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills
  • Strong organizational and time-management abilities
  • Valid driver's license, auto insurance, and vehicle (required)
  • BA/BS degree (preferred)

 

What’s In It for You?

We know sales is a grind, but the rewards are real. Here’s what you get:

  • Uncapped earning potential with a competitive compensation plan
  • Comprehensive onboarding and industry-leading sales training
  • Continuous coaching from experienced local leadership
  • Career advancement opportunities within one of America's leading media companies
  • 3 weeks PTO + 9 paid holidays (including 2 personal days)
  • Volunteer Time Off—give back to your community
  • Health, Dental, Vision, and Pet Insurance
  • 401(k) with company match + Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Company-provided laptop

 

More Than a Job. Build your future. Build your community. Build something extraordinary—with Townsquare Media Grand Rapids.

When you join Townsquare Media Grand Rapids, you're joining a team that celebrates big wins, supports one another, embraces innovation, and believes local businesses deserve world-class marketing.
You'll help launch new ideas, work with recognizable brands, attend exciting community events, collaborate with talented teammates, and build a career where your effort directly impacts your success.
If you're looking for a place where your ambition is rewarded, your ideas matter, and no two days are ever the same, we'd love to talk.

job.title: Digital Sales Manager
job.description:
Digital Sales Manager

*This is a full-time, in-office opportunity. *

 

Why Townsquare Media Group & Townsquare Ignite:

Townsquare is a media, entertainment, and digital marketing solutions company dedicated to serving small and mid-sized markets across the U.S. We own and operate 354 radio stations and more than 400 local websites across 74 markets, including trusted Tuscaloosa Stations..

We combine the power of local media with best-in-class digital solutions to help businesses grow—offering everything from broadcast and digital advertising to SEO, web design, and programmatic marketing.

 

Founded in 2010, Townsquare Ignite is the fastest-growing revenue and profit driver of Townsquare Media, offering a powerful suite of digital solutions that includes owned and operated digital properties, a proprietary programmatic advertising platform, and an in-house demand and data management platform powered by first-party data. Our all-in-one 360° advertising technology and DSP-agnostic trade desk provide access to all major ad exchanges and more than 250 billion impressions per day. Campaigns run across desktop, mobile, apps, connected TV, search, and social—supported by advanced targeting, white-glove service, and a full-service in-house creative team—giving sellers the tools, scale, and support to win and grow digital business.

 

The Digital Sales Manager Opportunity:

Do you love helping businesses grow through modern, results-driven marketing? Are you a sales leader who thrives in digital and knows how to elevate teams through strategy, coaching, and execution? This is a rare opportunity to lead a local market as a Digital Sales Manager, owning digital revenue growth while also leading and supporting broadcast sales performance.

 

At Townsquare, we are redefining local media by combining the power of trusted radio brands with industry-leading digital marketing solutions. We’re looking for a hands-on leader with deep digital sales expertise to accelerate growth across Townsquare Ignite and Amped (digital on our owned and operated properties), while maintaining strong broadcast fundamentals.

 

The Digital Sales Manager serves as the senior revenue leader for the market, responsible for driving total market performance with a digital-first mindset. This role blends digital strategy, team leadership, and client-facing sales execution. You will act as the market’s digital authority—guiding sellers, partnering with clients, and leading complex, integrated deals—while also overseeing broadcast sales activity.

 

Responsibilities:

Digital & Revenue Leadership

  • Own and drive digital revenue growth for the market, with a strong emphasis on Townsquare Ignite and Amped solutions
  • Develop and execute a digital-forward sales strategy that aligns broadcast and digital into integrated, results-based programs
  • Set, track, and hold the team accountable to digital and total revenue goals, pipeline activity, and KPIs
  • Lead by example in selling complex digital and integrated campaigns, assisting Account Executives with high-impact opportunities
  • Drive new business development while expanding and retaining key accounts

Digital Strategy & Expertise

  • Serve as the digital subject matter expert for the market
  • Lead adoption and mastery of full-funnel digital solutions including Programmatic, Search, Social, Video, OTT/CTV, and Owned & Operated digital
  • Analyze campaign performance and reporting to guide optimization, renewals, and incremental revenue growth
  • Translate performance data into clear, compelling insights for clients and sellers

Team Leadership & Development

  • Recruit, retain, and develop top-performing sales talent
  • Coach and train new and existing Account Executives on consultative selling, digital strategy, and solution-based presentations
  • Maintain a strong in-field presence, participating in client and prospect meetings alongside sellers
  • Set and enforce daily, weekly, and monthly activity, pipeline, and performance standards

Market & Community Leadership

  • Represent Townsquare as a trusted marketing partner to key clients, agencies, and community stakeholders
  • Monitor competitive activity and evolving market trends to identify growth opportunities
  • Act as a key member of the local leadership team

 

Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of sales management experience in digital and/or broadcast media
  • Extensive experience selling digital marketing solutions including Programmatic, Search, Social, Video, and OTT/CTV
  • Proven track record of driving digital revenue growth and exceeding sales targets
  • Strong understanding of full-funnel digital marketing strategies and performance metrics
  • Experience setting, tracking, and enforcing sales KPIs and revenue goals
  • Demonstrated success in consultative selling and complex deal execution
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and proposal development skills
  • Radio or broadcast experience is a plus, but not required
  • Website and owned-and-operated digital sales experience a plus
  • Valid Driver’s License and insurance

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive base plus performance-based bonus 
  • 3 weeks PTO + 9 paid holidays
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Company-provided laptop
  • Company discounts, pet insurance, and volunteer time off

job.title: Director of Digital & Radio Content - Fort Collins
job.description:
Director of Digital & Radio Content – Fort Collins

*This is a full-time, in-office opportunity. *

 

Where Creative Leadership Meets Local Impact:

Are you a strategic, people-first content leader with a passion for building winning brands and developing top-tier talent? At Townsquare Media Group, we’re looking for a Director of Digital & Radio Content to lead our MARKET market—overseeing strong local brands and driving audience growth across on-air, digital, social, and live platforms.

This is a full-time, in-office leadership role working closely and collaboratively with a talented local team. You’ll set the vision for local content, coach and develop market-leading talent, and play a hands-on role in creating compelling, clickable, and shareable content that resonates with the local community—while partnering closely with sales and leadership to drive revenue and impact.

 

Why Townsquare Media?

Townsquare is a media, entertainment, and digital marketing solutions company dedicated to serving small and mid-sized markets across the U.S. We own and operate 354 radio stations and more than 400 local websites across 74 markets—including trusted Fort Collins stations.

We combine the power of local media with best-in-class digital solutions to help businesses grow—offering everything from broadcast and digital advertising to SEO, web design, and programmatic marketing.

 

What You’ll Do:

As Director of Digital & Radio Content for Fort Collins, you’ll provide leadership, strategy, and creative direction for our local brands—ensuring excellence across on-air, online, and on-site experiences. This role blends high-level strategy with hands-on leadership and content creation. You will:

  • Establish and execute a clear, competitive vision for local content while maintaining ownership of the overall sound, content strategy, and brand execution across all stations to drive audience growth, market leadership, and business results.
  • Lead from the front as an active influencer, content creator, and brand ambassador, setting the standard for audience engagement while coaching team members to build meaningful connections across on-air, digital, social, and live platforms.
  • Recruit, develop, coach, and retain high-performing on-air, digital, and production talent, fostering a positive, collaborative, high-performance culture that drives market-leading results across all brands.
  • Partner closely with sales leadership and cross-functional teams to develop compelling, revenue-generating content, sponsorships, promotions, features, and events, creating innovative marketing solutions for clients while ensuring alignment across programming, sales, production, and market leadership.
  • Develop innovative, multi-platform content strategies that build highly engaged audience communities, drive ratings and digital growth, cultivate strong relationships throughout the market, and create revenue-generating partnerships across all channels.
  • Host a live, engaging on-air show on a regular, ongoing basis, preparing daily content that entertains, informs, and connects with the target audience
  • Create and publish a minimum of two original local articles per day for the station website and mobile app

  • Creating and publishing original video content regularly, including social-first short-form video (Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts) and longer-form segments that grow your personal on-screen brand
  • Prospecting and developing endorsement and influencer partnerships with local businesses, pitching yourself as a trusted community voice who can authentically promote products and services across on-air, video, and social platforms

What You’ll Bring:

  • Strong writing, communication, and storytelling skills across platforms
  • Familiarity with a wide range of digital assets, tools, and publishing workflows
  • Proven ability to lead in competitive markets and drive measurable results
  • Strong business acumen and the ability to connect content strategy to revenue outcomes
  • Sound judgment, creativity, and a strong desire to win

We know leadership roles come with high expectations—and we back that up with meaningful rewards:
